candidate_decisions.reason: The pericope supplies a clear remnant in 29:35, visible aftermath in 29:38, and Moses' delivered clear proofs in 29:39. The HFT trace gives a concrete before/after shift from a warning addressed to the rulers to a two-sided disclosure in which refusal can itself leave evidence for later viewers. The unresolved marker branch remains explicitly attributed to the supplied HFT trace.

The adjacent 29:38 sequence joins embellished conduct, diversion from a path, and retained insight, while 29:39 joins clear proofs to self-exalting response. All six traced branches have distinct carriers and are retained as a qualified contextual shift: perception remains available while valuation redirects it.

The focus locates self-exaltation in the land-domain and denies escape, while the immediately following 29:40 names seizure by offense and differentiated earth and water captures. The repeated earth carrier and the capture carriers land every supplied branch in a qualified territorial-reversal finding; the simple punishment-catalogue reading remains contained as an alternative.

The focus supplies a pursued party that cannot get ahead, and 29:40 supplies both culpable offense and the next-verse seizure. The supplied tail-or-end branch creates a materially distinct exploratory analogy in which consequence stays attached behind the runner; its stated boundary keeps that analogy from becoming the translation.

The focus arrival is explicitly paired with the next verse's drowning image. The supplied trace gives an independent water-gathering carrier, the ordinary presentation carrier, and the enclosure trigger, producing a bounded exploratory material analogy while preserving the ordinary account of Moses bringing proofs.

findings.title: Warning becomes residue
findings.claim: Within the pericope, the clear proofs before the rulers can be read as the first side of a disclosure whose other side is the clear remnant left after destruction.
findings.mechanism: The exact 29:35 anchor leaves a clear sign from the destroyed settlement, 29:38 makes the former dwellings visibly legible, and 29:39 places Moses' delivered proofs before the rulers' arrogance. The repeated disclosure carrier and the sequence from delivery to refusal connect warning evidence with aftermath evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The proofs become part of an evidentiary cycle: what is shown before refusal and what remains after it can both address a later viewer.
findings.containment: This adds a pericope-level relation to the ordinary account of Moses bringing proofs. The supplied source itself leaves open that the passages are independent examples rather than a designed cycle, and the exact Arabic anchors do not independently verify the HFT's segmentation or root assignments.

epistemic.reason: The changed reading is explicitly supplied by a visible HFT nomination and supported by exact Arabic anchors, but its cross-ayah mechanism and unresolved marker branch remain attributed rather than independently established.

findings.title: Sight redirected
findings.claim: The pericope permits the rulers' sight to remain active while embellished valuation and self-ranking redirect their discernment away from the disclosed path.
findings.mechanism: 29:38 places making conduct appear good before turning people from an extended path and describes them as possessing insight; 29:39 then places clear proofs before the self-exalting response. The adjacent sequence changes the refusal from simple inability to see into motivated redirection after disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus response becomes intelligible as obstruction despite perceptual capacity: evidence can be clear and still be redirected by the way it is valued.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading that the rulers reject clear proofs remains intact. The packet supports carrying the 29:38 mechanism into the focus by adjacency, while leaving open that 29:38 describes only the earlier peoples and does not diagnose the three named rulers.

epistemic.reason: The exact adjacent Arabic and six-role HFT trace support a specific changed reading, but the transfer of the 29:38 diagnosis to 29:39 is an attributed contextual inference.

findings.title: Territory turns into capture
findings.claim: The land-domain in which the rulers display greatness can, in the next ayah, become one of the created media through which their attempted escape is enclosed.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries self-exaltation in the earthly domain and denies the status of those able to outstrip. 29:40 binds seizure to offense and distributes capture through earth sinking and drowning. The repeated earth carrier and the differentiated capture media produce a spatial reversal across the verse boundary.
findings.reader_payoff: Earth becomes more than a neutral stage beneath power: the focus claim of territorial mastery is answered by a world that can participate in confinement.
findings.containment: The plain account remains that the rulers acted arrogantly on earth and could not escape. The packet also supports a simple punishment catalogue; it does not assign any particular capture mode to any named ruler, and the context branch roles are HFT attributions.

epistemic.reason: Immediate exact Arabic supports the earth/capture contact and the HFT trace supplies the before/after reversal, while root assignments for the lean next-ayah context remain attributed.

findings.reader_payoff: Consequence gains a physical shape: the one who runs ahead carries behind the very end that allows capture to catch up.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory material analogy, not the translation of the offense word and not a replacement for the ordinary causal reading that each is seized for an offense. The tail branch is the supplied outlier, and the packet's exact Arabic anchors do not independently establish its segmentation.

epistemic.reason: The outlier has a concrete focus pursuit carrier, an immediate next-ayah trigger, and an explicit boundary, but its tail facet is an unresolved exploratory nomination.

findings.title: Proofs as waymarks
findings.claim: With the explicitly added Fātiḥa ayat held as an overlay, the clear proofs in the focus can also be perceived as waymarks that orient movement along a straight road.
findings.mechanism: The focus clear-proof carrier meets the individually supplied 1:2 cue of a mark that distinguishes and guides, and 1:6 supplies the straight-road contact. The external material therefore changes the function felt in the focus from evidence alone to evidence with directional use, while returning through the focus proof occurrence.
findings.reader_payoff: The proofs acquire a navigational detail: their clarity can serve orientation, so refusal appears as a failure to let disclosed evidence direct movement.
findings.containment: This is a phase-two overlay, not a whole-Fātiḥa or surah thesis and not a claim that the focus is a prayer for guidance. The focus remains Moses bringing clear proofs and the rulers' arrogant response; only the supplied 1:2 and 1:6 local cues are used, and the external context branches are compact attributed cues.

epistemic.reason: The finding is an authoring inference from exact focus evidence and the individually supplied external branch cues; no HFT or independent support record is attached to the overlay.
